title: Opaque keyring Terraform module for secrets federation and HSM-backed rotation
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a reusable Terraform module that provisions an "opaque" keyring abstraction to unify HSM-backed keys and cloud KMS keys for Redwood Private deployments. The module must support dual-write federation to Secrets Manager and Vault, automated rotation with canary promotion, and lightweight runtime health probes so the control plane can detect degraded key material or sync failures. This is intended for on-prem and VPC customers who require HSM-backed signing keys with centralized secrets management and predictable upgrade/rotation behavior.

Scope:
- Terraform module (root-level) that creates keyring resources, KMS provider bindings, Vault mount + auth resources, and optional cloud-secrets dual-write role.
- Lifecycle hooks for safe upgrades: dual-write enable/disable flags, staged key promotion, and migration helper outputs for operators.
- Healthcheck Lambda/agent terraform resources that emit metrics to CloudWatch/Prometheus and a readiness probe configuration for the private control plane.
- Test harness examples and an ops runbook for rotations and emergency rollback.

Non-Goals:
- Replacing Vault operator; we will depend on existing Vault modules for core Vault server provisioning.
- Implementing bespoke HSM firmware-level integration; module should support common HSM providers via PKCS#11 or cloud HSM gateways.

If implemented well, this will reduce customer onboarding time for Private deployments, reduce incidents during key rotations, and give Platform teams a repeatable safe path for upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes variables to select: hsm_provider (none|cloud-hsm|pkcs11-gateway), enable_dual_write (true|false), rotation_policy (automatic|manual), and healthcheck_enabled (true|false)
Module can create Vault transit mount + named key and configure a Vault role that Redwood services can use; docs demonstrate auth method configuration
Module can configure cloud KMS key with IAM binding for dual-write, and outputs a stable key identifier for runtime use

Rotation workflow: canary key pair can be generated, traffic switched to canary for a subset of requests, metrics validate no regressions, and final promotion performed by terraform apply with documented steps
Healthchecks: a small probe (Lambda or sidecar) verifies key material accessibility, signs a test nonce via HSM/KMS, and emits success/failure metric; probe failures trigger an alert playbook
Upgrade safety: module supports a safe_flag that prevents destructive replacements by default and emits migration hints in outputs
Integration tests: example environment in test-harness runs module end-to-end against a soft-HSM (pkcs11 teststub) and Vault dev server with pass criteria
Documentation: README with architecture diagram, variables/outputs list, ops runbook for rotation and emergency rollback, and links to security review notes

notes: Implementation plan: 1) module scaffold + variables/outputs 2) health probe terraform resources 3) dual-write example and runbook 4) tests and docs 5) security review and release

Operator UX: include a `migration_plan` output that enumerates steps (create canary, enable dual-write, shift traffic %, validate metrics, promote, disable old key) so automation scripts can consume it
Risk: HSM vendor differences - mitigate by supporting a well-documented PKCS#11 shim and a cloud-hsm mode that delegates to provider-specific keys
Estimated follow-ups: automated canary promotion pipeline (CI job) and an RBAC hardening ticket under PM backlog
